headline: Looted weapons used in crimes, hundreds of escaped prisoners still at large after July uprising
summary: A significant number of firearms and ammunition looted during the July 2024 mass uprising remain unrecovered, with some now used in criminal activities. Hundreds of escaped prisoners, including death row inmates and militants, are also still at large, raising
details: A shotgun, confirmed to be among those looted from Araihaazar Police Station during the July 2024 mass uprising, was recently found in a fisherman's net in Singarpur, Narayanganj. This discovery highlights the ongoing issue of unrecovered weapons and the potential for their use in criminal activities.

Police officials confirm that a significant portion of the arms and ammunition looted from various police stations and prisons during the uprising are still in the hands of criminals. Disturbingly, evidence has also emerged of police members being involved in the sale of these stolen weapons.

According to Police Headquarters, 5,763 firearms and 652,008 rounds of ammunition were looted from police units nationwide following the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024. These included various types of rifles, SMGs, LMGs, pistols, shotguns, and tear gas munitions.

Joint operations launched on September 4, 2024, have so far recovered 4,445 firearms and 394,869 rounds of ammunition as of July 5 this year. This means 1,318 firearms and 257,139 rounds of ammunition are still unrecovered.

Concurrently, during the July uprising, 2,240 prisoners escaped from various correctional facilities, with 683 still at large. Among the escapees, 60 are death row inmates and 9 are identified militants, posing a significant threat to public safety.

The Director General of Prisons stated that 20 shotguns and Chinese rifles looted from prisons also remain unrecovered. While acknowledging that some high-risk escapees are being apprehended, he expressed concern over the overall law and order situation in the country.

Past incidents underscore the danger: a pistol looted from Chittagong Metropolitan Police's Kotwali Police Station was used in a double murder in Satkania, Chittagong, in March last year. A police constable was later arrested for his involvement in selling this weapon.

Another case involved a gang leader arrested in Chittagong in June last year with a pistol looted from Pahartali Police Station. This weapon was reportedly used by him and his associates in various crimes, including snatching and robbery. Several other criminals have also been arrested for using looted firearms in murders and extortion.

headline_marked: [[Samanzar Sayeed to represent Bangladesh]] at 75th Miss World in Vietnam
headline: Samanzar Sayeed to represent Bangladesh at 75th Miss World in Vietnam
summary: Samanzar Sayeed, crowned Miss World Bangladesh 2026, is set to compete on the global stage, expressing both surprise and determination to proudly represent her nation.
details: Samanzar Sayeed, recently crowned Miss World Bangladesh 2026, is preparing to fly to Vietnam to represent Bangladesh at the 75th Miss World global competition. The prestigious event is scheduled to commence on Sunday in Hanoi, Vietnam.

Sayeed expressed her excitement and surprise, stating she never imagined having the opportunity to stand on such a stage, despite enjoying beauty pageants since childhood. She aims to present herself confidently and showcase her abilities without nervousness.

A graduate of Biochemistry and Biotechnology from North South University, Sayeed initially entered the Miss World Bangladesh competition out of curiosity. She registered in July after graduating in April and was surprised to win the crown on her first attempt.

Following her victory, Sayeed underwent extensive grooming for personality development and international presentation. This experience significantly boosted her confidence and taught her how to better present herself, interacting with people from diverse backgrounds.

She emphasized that the competition is not solely about beauty but also about showcasing personality, thoughts, and social responsibility. Sayeed has a diverse range of interests, including Kathak and Bharatnatyam dance, singing, and various sports like basketball and table tennis.

Samanzar Sayeed was announced as Miss World Bangladesh 2026 on July 11, succeeding Aklima Atika Konika. Swagata Saha was the first runner-up, and Labiba Manjur was the second runner-up, with Ayesha Rahman and Yukta Bhoumik completing the top five.
The Miss World 2026 competition is scheduled to conclude on September 5 in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Sayeed hopes to pursue her hobbies and potentially acting after the competition.
